title: data-access-limited-use-and-audit-scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratch for redlining customer audit & data access clauses. Keep tight — win the ask without opening broad forensic access.

Top-line goals:
- Limit scope of any customer audits to specific logs/metrics tied to the customer tenant only. No blanket access to infra logs.
- Define frequency & notice window (e.g., quarterly with 14 days notice) and reasonable time-of-day constraints.
- Carve out privileged data (other tenants, platform PII, internal secrets, raw kernel/host logs).
- Customer pays for on-site/forensic effort beyond simple remote queries.
- For security incidents, require joint working group and mutual NDAs for any forensic deep dives.

Redline playbook (phrasing + alternatives):
- Customer requested: "Right to audit, inspect and copy logs and systems as necessary to verify compliance."
  - Counter: Replace with "Right to request and receive, subject to Redwood's reasonable review and redaction, copies of Customer-specific service logs and metrics necessary to demonstrate compliance with the Service Agreement."
  - Rationale: avoids access to underlying host/system logs and cross-tenant data.

- Scope definition to add: "Customer-specific telemetry" = logs, request traces, billing token usage, and model invocation metadata directly associated with customer's account ID. Exclude: host OS logs, node-level diagnostics, other customers' identifiers, and internal telemetry.

- Frequency & notice: propose "No more than once per calendar quarter; Customer must provide at least 14 business days' notice. Access windows: Redwood business hours PST unless otherwise agreed."

- On-site / Forensic clause: "If audit requires on-site presence, active Puppeteer/forensic tooling, or collection beyond provided artifacts, Customer will reimburse Redwood at Redwood's standard professional services rates; Redwood may require a written scope and statement of purpose prior to execution."

- Data minimization & redaction: "Redwood will remove or obfuscate all information that is not Customer-specific or that is necessary to protect other customers or Redwood's confidential information. Where possible, Redwood will provide sampled or aggregated artifacts and a signed attestation describing the process and the substitutions made."

- Escrow for logs: customer asked about escrow/archive. Quick stance: allow negotiated archival export for defined retention window and export format; require explicit SOW and extra fee. Do not agree to indefinite escrow or host-level snapshots.

- Subprocessors / subcontractors: require prior notice for any access to audit artifacts by subprocessors; allow redaction if subprocessors process other customers' data. Demand SOC2/ISO evidence in place rather than broad audit rights to subcontractor environments.

Negotiation talking points (short scripts):
- "We can certainly provide the artifacts you need to validate compliance. To protect our other customers and our platform security, we provide customer-scoped logs and signed attestations rather than full system access. If you need deeper forensic work, we can scope that under a paid SOW and do it together."
- "We prefer quarterly audits with reasonable notice so we can schedule an engineer and prepare an appropriately redacted artifact set."
- "For on-site or host-level artifacts we need a formal statement of work — those investigations are operationally heavy and must be priced."

Escalation / walkaway triggers (personal guiding lines):
- Ask to walk away or escalate to legal if: customer insists on unfettered, real-time access to host machines, raw kernel logs, or cross-tenant datasets.
- Escalate if customer requires indefinite retention of host-level snapshots or complete VM images.
- Push back hard if customer requires audit frequency > monthly with no cost responsibility.

Fallback concessions (what we can offer):
- Signed attestation from Redwood's security team (including SOC2/ISO statements) plus customer-scoped logs and sample request traces.
- Limited, time-boxed joint investigation with an agreed SOW and cost share.
- Marketplace of redacted artifacts + summary report instead of full copies.

Open questions to resolve with Legal (add before sending redline):
- Minimum wording to prove we satisfy e-discovery / regulatory customers (finance, healthcare) without exposing infra?
- Does Redwood have a standard reimbursable ratecard for on-site forensic investigations? Where is it stored?
- What are acceptable SLAs for turnaround on ad hoc log requests (24h, 3 business days)?

Quick checklist before sending counterparty redline:
- Insert defined "Customer-specific telemetry" definition.
- Add frequency + notice window.
- Add cost/responsibility language for elevated investigations.
- Add explicit exclusions (host logs, other customers, internal secrets).
- Insert redaction/minimization commitments and signed attestation option.
- Confirm team (SRE + Security) can deliver artifacts in proposed window.

Notes to self / negotiation tactics:
- Start with a firm but collaborative tone. Offer alternatives rather than flat no.
- Use SOC2 reports & redacted samples as trust-building first step.
- If customer is security team of enterprise, ask for their minimum acceptable artifacts and map to our logs — find common ground.
- Keep Legal looped but avoid legal-heavy responses on first reply; product/security voice works better initially.

Remember: goal is to limit operational exposure, set clear cost boundaries, and preserve our ability to protect other tenants.

Last-minute snippets to copy into counterproposal e-mail:
- "We can provide customer-scoped logs, redacted traces, and a signed attestation within 10 business days of receipt of a written request. For broader forensic analysis requiring host-level data or on-site access, we propose a scoped SOW and professional services engagement."
- "Audit frequency limited to quarterly, with 14 business days' written notice; additional requests handled via SOW and billed at Redwood professional services rates."

Unresolved small items (tack on migration to PRD later):
- Formalize professional services hourly/day rates and approval process.
- Template attestation language to reuse across deals.
- Add an internal playbook step: when customer requests audit, open JIRA ticket and tag security+sre with a standard template.
